llm_response: No—over-the-counter antifungal creams are a standard, effective first-line treatment for most cases of athlete’s foot when used as directed [1]. Common topical options include clotrimazole, miconazole, terbinafine, and tolnaftate, which are applied to the skin and typically used for 1 to 6 weeks to kill the fungus or slow its growth [1]. For more severe or persistent cases, prescription topical antifungals (such as ketoconazole, butenafine, or naftifine) or oral antifungal pills may be required, but creams and other topical agents are usually tried first and often work well if the full course is completed and foot hygiene is maintained [1]. While some products like tea tree oil are sometimes used, they may reduce symptoms without fully eradicating the infection, so proven antifungal medicines remain the recommended approach [1]. A shower-use antifungal wash exists as an alternative or complement to other treatments, but standard guidance still emphasizes established antifungal medications for primary therapy, [0, 1].
